responsibility: This module is the GNU Fortran front end and driver support for GCC. It covers the full language-specific compilation pipeline from source intake through lowering to GCC GENERIC: scanning and optional preprocessing (`scanner`, `cpp`), statement and expression parsing (`match`, `matchexp`, `primary`, `decl`, `parse`), symbol tables, namespaces, modules, and interface management (`symbol`, `module`, `interface`), semantic resolution and diagnostics (`resolve`, `check`, `error`, `options`), compile-time evaluation and language semantics such as arithmetic, arrays, constructors, DATA/EQUIVALENCE/COMMON, intrinsic procedures, polymorphism, coarrays, I/O, and OpenMP/OpenACC (`arith`, `array`, `constructor`, `data`, `dependency`, `intrinsic`, `iresolve`, `class`, `coarray`, `io`, `openmp`). In localization terms, resolve/check files decide whether parsed Fortran symbols, assignments, calls, allocation expressions, and procedure interfaces are semantically valid, while `trans*`, `convert`, and `f95-lang` files map already-resolved declarations, expressions, arrays, constants, intrinsics, common blocks, I/O, and parallel constructs into GCC backend trees and runtime calls. The build/spec/options/manual files define how gfortran is built, invoked, documented, and linked against libgfortran. Overall, this module implements Fortran language parsing, semantic analysis, intrinsic and module semantics, and translation into GCC's middle-end representation, distinguishing it from target back ends and middle-end optimization modules.
